summary: Mapped ticker relationships for the Consumer candidate chunk around value staples, foodservice packaging, repair/remodel, specialty building-products distribution, manufactured housing, and housing-affordability derivatives. Key public-market hygiene update: AZEK, BECN, and DOOR should not survive as standalone tickers because AZEK was acquired by James Hardie, Beacon Roofing Supply was acquired by QXO, and Masonite was acquired by Owens Corning. The strongest underfollowed relationships in this chunk are manufactured housing affordability exposure through CVCO and SKY, non-discretionary or insurance-linked exterior repair exposure through legacy BECN now inside QXO, and second-order repair/remodel distribution or components through SITE, PATK, FBIN, and BLDR. FLO and KRT remain lower-evidence consumer staples/foodservice infrastructure hypotheses requiring segment, customer, and margin validation.
